abstract: Fulminant viral myocarditis (FVM) is characterized by acute onset and rapid progression, often deteriorating into cardiogenic shock, malignant arrhythmias, and multi-organ failure within days. Its pathological essence does not lie in the "quantitative accumulation" of focal lymphocytic infiltration seen in ordinary myocarditis, but rather in a "qualitative shift" driven by diffuse myocardial edema compounded by a multi-cytokine cascade. Accumulating evidence indicates that the "inflection point" of myocardial injury is determined not by viral load per se, but by the dysregulated pattern recognition of viral antigens by the innate immune system and the resultant imbalance of the inflammatory network. The organising framework of this review is temporal (hyperacute to acute to reparative immune states). A spatial dimension, contrasting the circulating and the cardiac-resident immune compartments, is developed wherever direct or closely analogous data exist, but it carries far less evidence than the temporal dimension and is treated as secondary to it. Myocarditis that is immune-mediated without a replicating cardiotropic virus, including vaccine-associated and checkpoint-inhibitor disease, is used here as a labelled comparator and not as part of the entity under review. The virus invades cardiomyocytes and vascular endothelium via receptors with non-canonical distribution, subsequently triggering type I interferon responses and necroptosis through endosomal and cytosolic pattern-recognition receptors, and initiating a cascade effect via damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). The driver of cardiomyocyte death does not stay constant across this course: virus-intrinsic cytopathic and ferroptotic death predominates in the first days, myeloid-mediated killing takes over through the remainder of the first week, and cytotoxic lymphocytes become the principal effectors thereafter. The hyperacute phase is characterized by macrophage phenotypic drift, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and a "cytokine storm" whose earliest cellular sources in viral myocarditis are myeloid rather than T-cell derived. The acute phase features the "clearance-injury" paradox of cytotoxic T cells and the failure of immune checkpoint regulation, and a subset of patients may subsequently follow what the authors describe as a candidate immunoparalysis trajectory rather than an established third stage of disease - a state provisionally characterized by regulatory T cell (Treg) expansion, paradoxical elevation of interleukin-10 (IL-10), and downregulation of monocyte human leukocyte antigen-DR (HLA-DR). Its reported association with secondary infection and adverse outcome derives largely from sepsis and critical-care cohorts and has not been demonstrated in FVM. Building on this "inflammatory time window," the authors propose a phase-specific framework intended to generate hypotheses rather than to recommend treatment: in the hyperacute phase, "fire-extinguishing" approaches (complement blockade and cytokine adsorption) may represent a potential alternative to broad-spectrum immunosuppression; in the acute phase, selective blockade of individual pathways according to inflammatory subtype may be worth exploring; and in the reparative phase, measures aimed at restoring regulatory immune capacity may be considered for study. None of these pathways, and none of the biomarker values discussed in the main text, has been prospectively validated in FVM. Finally, this review envisions individualized decision-making guided by multi-omics and dynamic immune monitoring, emphasizing that the prognosis of FVM depends on the capacity for "dynamic phenotyping and real-time switching" of immune status, rather than reliance on any single therapeutic modality.
title: From cytokine storm to adaptive dysregulation: temporal evolution of the inflammatory network and phase-specific intervention strategies in fulminant viral myocarditis.

abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) leads to considerable morbidity and mortality worldwide. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is an imaging modality to guide percutaneous coronary intervention; however, it requires time-consuming, expert-dependent manual analysis. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly used for IVUS analysis, but there is limited evidence on its diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility. This review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical usefulness of AI for automated IVUS analysis of coronary arteries. The research protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO, CRD420261454806) and followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines for systematic reviews. PubMed/MEDLINE and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through July 23, 2026, and July 26, 2026, respectively, for publications assessing AI, machine learning, or deep learning algorithms for the automated analysis of coronary IVUS, including segmentation of structures, identification of plaque types, and quantitative measurements. Two reviewers independently screened and selected eligible studies and extracted the data. The risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 (Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) and visualized using robvis, and the GRADE approach was used to rate the certainty of evidence. Of the 802 records identified (PubMed, n = 216; Cochrane CENTRAL, n = 586), eight studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in this review. They reported on the performance of convolutional neural networks, U-Net/U-Net++, Efficient-UNet, DeepLabv3+-based models, and gradient boosting in segmenting lumen, vessel, plaque, and stent in coronary IVUS. The Dice similarity coefficient ranged from 0.67 to 0.97, and the intersection over union for segmentation (including Jaccard similarity) ranged from 0.66 to 0.97, with the best performance for lumen and vessel segmentation and the poorest for stent and calcium. The sensitivity and specificity ranged from 62% to 90% and 88% to 99%, respectively, with the correlation to expert assessment generally above 0.9. Overall, the risk of bias was mainly related to patient selection (five out of eight studies) and the reference standard (three out of eight studies), and none of the studies was rated as having a high risk of bias. Due to between-study heterogeneity in the tasks, reference standards, and outcome measures, a meta-analysis was not performed, and the certainty of evidence was rated as low. The current evidence suggests that AI-based methods have good potential for analyzing coronary IVUS with acceptable accuracy, which could be helpful for high-throughput IVUS interpretation in clinical practice. They appear to perform best at segmenting lumen and vessel structures and worst at segmenting stent and calcium. However, due to the overall low certainty of evidence from these mostly retrospective studies, their use should be limited to complementing the work of experts in cardiovascular medicine.
title: Artificial Intelligence for Automated Analysis and Interpretation of Intravascular Ultrasound in Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population.
METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the prospective China DVD2 multicenter cohort, 298 patients with isolated severe AR who underwent TAVR were included. Frailty was assessed preprocedurally using an abbreviated 8-9-item cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) encompassing functional, cognitive, nutritional, and clinical domains. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. The cohort-derived FI threshold for mortality was derived using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP were applied. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed.
RESULTS: The cohort-derived FI threshold was 0.407, classifying 32 patients as high frailty. High-FI patients exhibited greater symptom burden, higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, larger left atrial diameter, and elevated NT-proBNP. One-year mortality was significantly higher in the high-FI group compared with low-FI patients (15.6% vs 3.4%, P = 0.010). High FI was associated with higher one-year mortality in Model 3 (HR 4.00, 95% CI 1.18-13.50; P = 0.026). No significant multiplicative or additive interaction with NT-proBNP was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing TAVR for severe native aortic regurgitation, a high FI was associated with higher one-year mortality. These findings extend prior evidence on the prognostic implications of frailty to this understudied population.
title: Prognostic Value of the Frailty Index in Patients with Severe Aortic Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adding milrinone to dobutamine (dobutamine-milrinone escalation) in cardiogenic shock (CS) is reimbursed for a limited duration under Indonesia's national health insurance, but the cost structure of escalation remains poorly characterized. This study quantified direct medical charges associated with escalation and the contribution of drug acquisition.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Retrospective cohort of 76 adult CS survivors (20 escalation, 56 dobutamine monotherapy) at Indonesia's national cardiovascular referral center, 2020-2024. Covariate Balancing Propensity Score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting, using pre-treatment covariates, estimated adjusted cost ratios (CR) for intensive cardiovascular care unit (ICVCU) and total hospital costs from institutional billing records.
RESULTS: Escalation was associated with higher ICVCU costs (CR 2.711; 95% CI 1.912-3.844; p < 0.001) and total hospital costs (CR 2.321; 95% CI 1.372-3.929; p = 0.002). Combined inotrope costs represented 4.3% of ICVCU expenditure in the escalation group, compared with 30.9% for therapeutic and interventional procedures. Baseline vasoactive-inotropic score correlated with total hospital cost (ρ=0.597; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Drug acquisition represented a minor share of costs associated with dobutamine-milrinone escalation. The findings support consideration of severity- and resource-based approaches to reimbursement rather than focusing solely on duration limits for individual inotropes. Interpretation is limited by the retrospective, single-center, survivor-only design.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Doppler echocardiography supports noninvasive hemodynamic assessment, but its interpretation may vary across acute heart failure syndromes. We compared Doppler filling patterns and their relationship with pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) and acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single-center observational study included 61 patients with ADHF (n = 34) or AMI-CS (n = 27) who underwent contemporaneous echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic assessment. Transmitral inflow, pulmonary venous flow, and tissue Doppler indices were compared between groups and analyzed in relation to PCWP. Exploratory ROC analyses assessed discrimination of PCWP ≥ 18 mmHg.
RESULTS: Patients with ADHF had greater cardiac chamber enlargement and higher mean PCWP than those with AMI-CS (24.7 ± 8.4 vs. 18.0 ± 5.4 mmHg; p < 0.001). ADHF was characterized by higher E/A (2.8 ± 1.2 vs. 1.3 ± 1.2; p < 0.001), lower pulmonary venous S/D (0.7 ± 0.5 vs. 1.1 ± 0.5; p < 0.01), and higher average E/e' (21.0 ± 7.3 vs. 12.5 ± 4.7; p < 0.001). Deceleration time did not differ significantly. Average and septal E/e' correlated with PCWP in the pooled cohort but not within either group separately. Septal E/e' yielded AUCs of 0.868 (95% CI, 0.722-1.000) in ADHF and 0.762 (95% CI, 0.511-1.000) in AMI-CS.
CONCLUSIONS: ADHF and AMI-CS exhibit distinct Doppler filling profiles alongside differences in invasive filling pressure and cardiac remodeling. These findings support contextual interpretation of Doppler indices during bedside hemodynamic assessment of critically ill patients. The diagnostic value of syndrome-specific interpretation requires independent validation.
title: Distinct Doppler echocardiographic patterns of elevated left ventricular filling pressure in acute decompensated heart failure and AMI-related cardiogenic shock: a simultaneous Doppler-hemodynamic study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) treats severe tricuspid regurgitation, but electrical complications from device-tissue interactions remain poorly characterized.
CASE SUMMARY: A 79-year-old woman developed postural ventricular arrhythmias after TriClip implantation. Electrocardiography was consistent with an ectopic origin in the posterior/inferior right ventricle, anatomically concordant with the posteroseptal clip. Orthostatic reduction in right ventricular volume may have induced dynamic clip-endocardium contact. Saline infusion abolished the arrhythmias. At 1 month, she remained asymptomatic despite unchanged device-to-septum distance on supine echocardiography, suggesting stabilization of the device-tissue interface over time.
DISCUSSION: As the first reported case of postural arrhythmia from mechanical TriClip-septal interaction, this addresses a gap in TEER literature regarding how orthostatic volume shifts trigger device-related complications.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Orthostatic volume shifts may provoke dynamic device-tissue contact and arrhythmias post-TEER. Careful clip positioning and vigilant postprocedural monitoring are essential, and stabilization of the device-tissue interface over time may allow conservative management.
title: Ventricular Arrhythmia After Percutaneous Edge-to-Edge Tricuspid Valve Repair.
Prognostic Value of TVARC-Based Right Ventricular Dysfunction Grading in Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The virtual circle method is currently used in preprocedural computed tomography planning for Redo-transcatheter aortic valve (TAV) replacement to simulate the predicted outer boundary of the index TAV and the valve-to-aorta distance for coronary risk assessment, yet its accuracy against postprocedural observations has not been evaluated. This study aimed to assess the accuracy of the virtual circle method in predicting index TAV expansion and coronary risk following a second TAV implantation using paired preprocedural and postprocedural computed tomography in patients undergoing Redo-TAV replacement.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 58 patients who underwent Redo-TAV replacement at 5 sites with paired preprocedural and postprocedural cardiac computed tomography. Three valve combinations were analyzed: Evolut-in-SAPIEN (n=17), SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN (n=13), and SAPIEN-in-Evolut (n=28). Index TAV frame expansion was quantified by area- or perimeter-derived diameter change. Accuracy of the virtual circle method was defined as a diameter difference within ±1 mm between predicted and observed index TAV frame diameter.
RESULTS: In the Evolut-in-SAPIEN combination, meaningful index SAPIEN frame expansion occurred only with effective pre/postdilatation, whereas in both the SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN and SAPIEN-in-Evolut combinations, consistent frame expansion was observed regardless of dilatation. Changes in index frame diameter corresponded inversely to changes in valve-to-aorta distance. In the SAPIEN-in-Evolut combination, expansion was governed chiefly by implant position and sizing strategy. Across all combinations in which the virtual circle method was applicable (n=53), accurate prediction was achieved in 31 patients (58.5%), with overestimation in 14 (26.4%) and underestimation in 8 (15.1%).
CONCLUSIONS: The virtual circle method provided an accurate or conservative (overestimating) estimate of index TAV expansion and coronary risk in the majority of patients (85%), supporting its clinical utility for Redo-TAVR planning. The remaining 15% showed underestimation of modest magnitude (median, 1.3 mm), occurring predominantly in patients who underwent predilatation and postdilatation, warranting heightened caution in borderline coronary anatomy when dilatation strategies are employed.
title: Accuracy of Virtual Circle Method and Valve-to-Aorta Distance Change After Redo-TAVR: Multicenter Paired CT Analysis.

abstract: Background: Bailout mechanical circulatory support (MCS) may be used in the setting of intraprocedural hemodynamic collapse during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We developed and externally validated a simple risk prediction model for bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI. Methods: Consecutive patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2025 were included in the derivation cohort (n=6,931), after excluding cases of salvage PCI and procedures performed with pre-existing or prophylactic MCS. The primary endpoint was bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse. A multivariable Firth logistic regression model was developed, internally validated, and translated into a simplified integer-based risk score (ORACLE). External validation was performed in 214,877 PCIs from the Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Cardiovascular Consortium (BMC2) registry. Results: The incidence of bailout MCS was 1.4% in the derivation cohort. Six variables (non-elective presentation, systolic blood pressure, chronic heart failure, prior PCI, rotational/orbital atherectomy, and left main PCI) independently predicted the primary endpoint. The regression model demonstrated good discrimination both in the derivation (area under the curve [AUC] 0.817; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.774-0.860) and external validation (AUC 0.761; 95% CI 0.753-0.770) cohorts. The simplified ORACLE score preserved most of the discriminatory performance of the full model (AUC 0.791 in the derivation cohort and 0.718 in the external validation cohort) and effectively stratified patients, with observed bailout MCS rates ranging from 0.4% in the low-risk category to 8.7% in the high-risk group, with similar findings in the external validation cohort. Discrimination was consistent across clinically relevant subgroups. Negative predictive value was >99% in both the derivation and external validation cohorts. Conclusions:: ORACLE is a simple score to estimate the risk of bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI, which may support preprocedural risk assessment.

abstract: Intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI. Contemporary coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides comprehensive assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque characteristics, vessel dimensions, calcification, and lesion-specific physiology, enabling detailed procedural planning before catheterisation. The Precise Procedural and PCI Plan (P4) trial is a prospective, international, multicentre, randomised, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication designed to determine whether a comprehensive CCTA-guided PCI strategy is non-inferior to intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes. Approximately 1,100 patients with chronic coronary syndromes or stabilised acute coronary syndrome, at least one coronary stenosis >70%, and fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA ≤0.80 are enrolled. Following central core laboratory confirmation of anatomical and physiological eligibility, patients are randomised 1:1 to CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI. Patients assigned to CCTA-guided PCI undergo standardised procedural planning and virtual PCI simulation, with CCTA integrated into the catheterisation laboratory using computed tomography-fluoroscopy synchronisation for intraprocedural guidance. In the IVUS-guided arm, PCI is performed with mandatory pre- and post-PCI IVUS assessment. The primary endpoint is target vessel failure at 12 months, defined as the composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven target vessel revascularisation. P4 will determine whether comprehensive, non-invasive CCTA-guided PCI planning is non-inferior to IVUS-guided PCI regarding 12-month target vessel failure while potentially improving procedural efficiency and standardisation. abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient).
AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment.
METHODS: Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index.
RESULTS: Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy remains the standard treatment following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). While prasugrel and ticagrelor offer consistent antiplatelet effects, they increase bleeding risk compared with clopidogrel, which requires CYP2C19 bioactivation.
AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of rapid CYP2C19 genotyping at the time of PCI on P2Y12 inhibitor selection and clinical outcomes in real-world patients.
METHODS: A total of 974 patients who underwent PCI and rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and received P2Y12 inhibitor treatment were included. P2Y12 inhibitor selection, P2Y12 inhibitor switching, major atherothrombotic events (MAE; a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, stent thrombosis, or unstable angina requiring revascularisation), and bleeding events were assessed throughout the first year post-PCI. Time-varying Cox regression analysis was performed to assess event risk in patients treated with clopidogrel (reference) versus prasugrel/ticagrelor after stratifying by loss-of-function (LOF) status and adjusting for stratum-specific confounders.
RESULTS: Clopidogrel was prescribed more frequently at discharge among CYP2C19 non-LOF versus LOF carriers (43% [296/691] vs 31% [87/283]; p<0.001). The median duration of follow-up was 359 days (interquartile range [IQR] 190-362 days). Among LOF allele carriers de-escalating to clopidogrel, the median de-escalation time was 180 days (IQR 92-354 days). MAE were not significantly different between P2Y12 inhibitor regimens after stratifying by LOF status (LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=147] vs LOF-clopidogrel [n=136]: adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.87 [95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.36-2.10]; non-LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=272] vs non-LOF-clopidogrel [n=419]: adjusted HR 1.26, 95% CI: 0.67-2.36). No significant differences in Bleeding Academic Research Consortium bleeding events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: This real-world study shows that, among LOF carriers managed with rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and delayed de-escalation, ischaemic and bleeding event rates were not significantly different between those taking clopidogrel versus those taking prasugrel/ticagrelor, though findings should be interpreted cautiously.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) physiological indices have prognostic relevance. Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) enables wire-free, rapid, single-view functional assessment, yet its long-term prognostic value after PCI remains incompletely established.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of post-PCI μQFR for long-term adverse outcomes.
METHODS: This prespecified subgroup analysis of the FAVOR III China trial included 3,825 patients. All PCI-treated vessels with a reference diameter ≥2.5 mm and 50-90% diameter stenosis were analysed for offline post-PCI μQFR. The primary endpoint was 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; including death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation).
RESULTS: Post-PCI μQFR was successfully analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients, with similar distributions between the randomised treatment groups. At 5 years, a low post-PCI μQFR was associated with a higher incidence of MACE compared with the intermediate and high post-PCI μQFR tertiles (23.1% vs 19.0% vs 17.2%; p=0.001). Using the highest tertile (μQFR>0.95) as a reference, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were 1.08 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87-1.34) for the intermediate tertile (0.92-0.95) and 1.30 (95% CI: 1.06-1.60) for the lowest tertile (μQFR ≤0.91). Using a receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, MACE occurred more frequently in patients with post-PCI μQFR <0.94 (22.3% vs 17.4%, aHR 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.47; p=0.02) than in those with post-PCI μQFR ≥0.94. No significant interaction was observed between treatment strategy and post-PCI μQFR (p for interaction=0.23).
CONCLUSIONS: Post-PCI μQFR distributions were similar between treatment groups, but lower values were associated with higher 5-year adverse event risk without significant treatment interaction. Its limited binary discrimination supports use as a continuous metric for post-PCI physiological risk stratification. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03656848).

abstract: This cross-sectional exploratory study investigates the potential of metabolomics to differentiate between stable coronary artery disease (CAD) and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) through Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopic analysis. The study identifies distinct metabolic profiles for each condition, revealing significant variations in metabolite levels, particularly lactic acid, which is a key metabolic product of anaerobic glycolysis, emerges as a prominent marker in AMI patients, reflecting acute ischemic stress and providing insight into adverse outcomes associated with high lactate levels. Another metabolite found in the present study was hypoxanthine, which is key biomarker for myocardial ischemia. These findings underscore the potential of metabolomics in combination with pathway analysis in distinguishing between CAD and AMI and highlight the metabolic dysregulation that occurs in these diseases. Our results suggest that these metabolites could serve as potential biomarkers, paving the way for personalized prognostic and diagnostic strategies. Further large-scale studies are necessary to validate these findings and incorporate them into clinical practice.
title: Metabolomic Analysis of Patients with Coronary Artery Disease and Acute Myocardial Infarction by Using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) carries high mortality. The impact of prosthetic valve type on outcomes remains unclear, particularly with the increasing use of transcatheter valves. We aimed to identify predictors of 30-day and 1-year mortality in PVE and assess the association between valve type and outcomes.
METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter cohort study, patients aged ≥ 18 years with definite or possible PVE from the Türkiye Endocarditis Group registry between January 2016 and December 2025 were included. Valve type was evaluated across three groups: mechanical PVE (mPVE), surgical bioprosthetic PVE (bPVE), and percutaneous bPVE. Cox proportional hazards models were used.
RESULTS: A total of 261 patients were included (median age 63 years [IQR 49-71], 37.9% female). Among patients with available follow-up data, the 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were 23.1% (58/251) and 46.3% (100/216), respectively. In multivariable analysis, age (HR 1.027 per year; 95% CI 1.006-1.049), creatinine level on admission (HR 1.154 per mg/dL; 95% CI 1.019-1.306), and cardiac complications (HR 3.589; 95% CI 2.080-6.193) were independently associated with 30-day mortality and remained significant for 1-year mortality. Valve type was not independently associated with mortality after adjustment for measured confounders. Enterococcus spp. were more frequent in percutaneous bPVE.
CONCLUSION: In this national multicenter cohort, PVE carried high mortality regardless of valve type. Older age, higher creatinine levels, and cardiac complications-but not valve type-were the strongest predictors of short- and long-term mortality. The higher frequency of Enterococcus spp. in percutaneous bPVE suggests that valve type may be more closely related to microbiological profile than prognosis.

abstract: Rapid progression of aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the myocardial changes accompanying faster progression remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between the rate of AS progression and myocardial fibrosis assessed by computed tomography (CT)-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV), and the impact on clinical outcomes. We studied 134 patients with classical high-gradient severe AS who underwent pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation cardiac CT with a delayed dual-energy acquisition for ECV quantification and had at least two echocardiograms ≥ 6 months apart. Progression was defined as the annualized change in peak aortic jet velocity. Rapid progression was defined as an increase > 0.30 m/s/year. Patients were followed for a composite of cardiovascular hospitalization, urgent aortic valve replacement, or death. ECV correlated with progression rate (Spearman ρ = 0.33, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, faster progression remained independently associated with ECV (β = 2.52, p = 0.001). Rapid progressors had higher ECV than slow progressors (31.5% vs. 28.3%, p < 0.001). Over a median follow-up of 16.2 months, 36 patients (26.9%) reached the composite outcome. Patients with both rapid progression and high ECV had an event rate of 69 versus 11 per 100 patient-years in those without (adjusted HR 6.22, 95% CI 3.13-12.32). Faster AS progression is independently associated with greater diffuse myocardial fibrosis, irrespective of stenosis severity, and their combination identified patients at higher risk of adverse events. These findings suggest that AS progression rate and myocardial tissue characterization carry complementary prognostic information in severe AS.

abstract: Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) is often the first clinical presentation of coronary artery disease. Current diagnostic standards rely on invasive coronary angiography (ICA) to guide therapy. Non-invasive coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) may currently be used to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease in low-risk NSTE-ACS. The recently introduced photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) may further expand its application in high-risk NSTE-ACS patients, as well. This review explores the current and emerging role of CCTA in the evaluation of patients with an established diagnosis of NSTE-ACS.

abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) practice for cardiogenic shock may vary with institutional resources and operator experience, but data from Japanese interventional cardiologists are limited. We conducted an anonymous cross-sectional survey of 720 members of 83 Japanese Association of Cardiovascular Intervention and Therapeutics (CVIT)-certified or affiliated training hospitals in the CVIT Kyushu-Okinawa Chapter (September-October 2025); 536 returned questionnaires (74.4%), and consent was confirmed for 385 (53.5%). The primary analysis included 276 respondents who had performed intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), or Impella CP insertion within 12 months: 163 at Impella-capable and 113 at non-Impella-capable hospitals. Documented MCS and extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation protocols were more frequently reported by respondents from Impella-capable hospitals (46% vs. 6% and 39% vs. 13%, respectively), as was collaboration with emergency and critical care physicians; no statistically significant difference was detected in perceived need for collaboration. MCS selection varied between groups. At Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock stage C, IABP (44%) and Impella CP (48%) were selected with similar frequency among respondents in Impella-capable hospitals, whereas IABP was selected by 79% in non-Impella-capable hospitals. At stage E, ECPELLA (79%) and VA-ECMO plus IABP (84%) predominated, respectively. Among respondents with device-specific operator experience within 12 months, vascular access and anticoagulation practices varied between groups. Procedural anxiety was lower with higher CVIT qualification; however, 19% of board-certified members reported anxiety about Impella CP insertion and 45% about emergency intubation. These findings identify MCS practice variation across several domains warranting further evaluation.

abstract: Prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is associated with accelerated native vessel atherosclerosis and more complex chronic total occlusion (CTO) anatomy, rendering CTO-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) more challenging despite contemporary technical advances. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare CTO lesion characteristics, procedural demands, and in-hospital outcomes according to prior CABG status. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were systematically searched from inception through May 15, 2026, for studies comparing CTO-PCI outcomes in patients with and without prior CABG. Data were pooled using odds ratios (ORs) and standardized mean differences (SMDs). Twelve studies enrolling 47,434 patients, including 10,354 with prior CABG, were included. Compared with patients without prior CABG, those with prior CABG had higher rates of blunt stump morphology (OR 1.51 [1.42-1.61]), proximal cap ambiguity (OR 1.55 [1.45-1.66]), calcification (OR 2.49 [2.22-2.79]), vessel bending (OR 2.27 [1.27-4.05]), distal cap bifurcation (OR 1.73 [1.51-1.98]), and higher Multicenter CTO Registry of Japan scores (SMD 0.48 [0.40-0.56]). Procedural burden was greater, with higher contrast use, longer fluoroscopy time and procedure duration, and greater stent use. Technical success (OR 0.63 [0.43-0.92]) and procedural success (OR 0.60 [0.53-0.69]) were lower in the prior CABG group. In-hospital mortality (OR 2.19), myocardial infarction (OR 2.29), and contrast-induced nephropathy (OR 1.97) were higher, whereas cardiac tamponade was less frequent (OR 0.37). Prior CABG is associated with substantially greater CTO complexity, procedural burden, and in-hospital risk, underscoring the need for careful procedural planning and individualized risk stratification in this population.
title: Prior Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Its Impact on Lesion Complexity, Procedural Characteristics, and Outcomes in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiofrequency renal denervation (RDN) is a guideline-recommended therapy for uncontrolled hypertension. SPYRAL AFFIRM is a single-arm, postapproval study assessing the efficacy and safety of radiofrequency RDN using the Symplicity Spyral catheter. We report the 6-month primary end point results in the SPYRAL AFFIRM US population.
METHODS: Enrolled patients had an office systolic/diastolic blood pressure (BP) ≥140/90 mm Hg and a home systolic BP ≥135 mm Hg. Patients with type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c >8.0%), or an estimated glomerular filtration rate <45 mL/min per 1.73 m2 were excluded. The primary end point was the 6-month change in office systolic BP from baseline compared with a prespecified performance goal (-6.0 mm Hg).
RESULTS: Among 594 patients treated in the AFFIRM study from 73 US clinical sites, baseline clinical characteristics included: mean (±SD) age, 57±12 years; female, 45%; African American, 27%; Hispanic, 11%; type 2 diabetes, 19%; and mean estimated glomerular filtration rate, 79±20 mL/min per 1.73m2. Baseline systolic/diastolic office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory BP (mm Hg) were 169±21/106±13, 158±17/101±13, and 151±18/96±13, respectively. Patients were prescribed an average of 3.6±2.0 antihypertensive medications at baseline that remained unchanged through 6 months. Six months after RDN, the change in systolic BP (mm Hg) was -18.2±22.0, -9.4±13.8, and -9.7±16.8 for office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory measures, respectively (P<0.001 compared with baseline). Adverse clinical events through 6 months were uncommon.
CONCLUSIONS: In this US postapproval study, the primary end point was met with significant BP reductions following radiofrequency RDN consistent across different measures. In a broader patient population with uncontrolled hypertension, these results reaffirm the safety and efficacy of radiofrequency RDN.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), asymmetric valve expansion can estimate prosthetic dysfunction and death. Postdilation has shown promising results in optimizing valve geometry in observational studies; however, randomized evidence is currently lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the efficacy of routine postdilation on transcatheter heart valve (THV) geometry and hemodynamic performance, and associated safety outcomes.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: DUOTAP was a single-center, single-blinded randomized clinical trial. Recruitment took place from January 2025 to April 2026 and end points were assessed periprocedurally (fluoroscopy) at 30 days (adverse events) and at 3 months (computed tomography [CT]). The trial was conducted at a high-volume tertiary referral center, the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. Included patients had severe AS suitable for transfemoral TAVI with a balloon-expandable THV and without high-risk features on preprocedural CT or coronary angiography and were randomized in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by THV size, to routine postdilation vs no postdilation. These data were analyzed from July 2026 to September 2026.
INTERVENTION: Routine postdilation using the original delivery balloon at the identical filling volume. A sham procedure was performed in the control group.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index served as primary end point. Further fluoroscopic and CT-derived measures of valve geometry, hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), paravalvular leak (PVL), and THV hemodynamics on echocardiography, and freedom from major procedural adverse events served as secondary end points.
RESULTS: Overall, 148 patients (median [IQR] age, 81 [77-85] years; 69 female [46.6%] and 79 male [53.4%]; median EuroSCORE-II, 2.3%) underwent randomization (n = 74 intervention vs n = 74 control). Intervention yielded a 70% lower THV asymmetry index compared with control (median: 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio: 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.47; P < .001), with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups, induced by frame height reduction across the outer curve. Additionally, intervention yielded numerically larger THV diameters on fluoroscopy and significantly larger THV areas at the inflow, midframe, and outflow level on CT. HALT and mild or worse PVL were significantly less frequent and the Doppler Velocity Index was significantly higher in the intervention group. No differences in procedure-related adverse events between groups were recorded (χ2 test: P = .36).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, postdilation led to reduced THV asymmetry, optimized geometry, and improved hemodynamic performance, without increasing procedure-related adverse events. These results support the use of routine postdilation to optimize THV geometry and hemodynamics in suitable patients.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty using the Cardioband system in a single-center cohort of high-risk patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation.
METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort study included 64 consecutive patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation undergoing transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty with the Cardioband system. Clinical and echocardiographic data were collected at baseline, discharge, 6-months, and 12-months. Primary endpoints included changes in tricuspid regurgitation severity, annular dimensions, and clinical status, as well as all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Outcomes were analyzed using available-case data.
RESULTS: At 12-months, among patients with available echocardiographic data (n = 44), tricuspid regurgitation severity was reduced compared with baseline (p < 0.001); 15.9% had trace or mild TR, 45.5% had moderate TR, 27.3% had severe TR, and 11.4% had massive or torrential TR. All-cause mortality at 12-months was 6.3% (4/64 patients). According to TVARC criteria, intraprocedural success was achieved in 81.3% of patients, while a more stringent definition yielded a success rate of 65.6%.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort of high-risk patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation, transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty using the Cardioband system was associated with reductions in tricuspid regurgitation severity and improvements in selected clinical parameters at 12-months. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the observational design, incomplete follow-up, and the absence of a control group, as well as the observed rate of procedural complications. Further studies, ideally including larger multicenter cohorts and controlled comparisons, are needed to better define the role of this therapy in the management of tricuspid regurgitation.
title: Clinical outcomes and coronary complication risk after transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty with cardioband: a 12-month single-center cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents has been widely used to treat patients with left main coronary artery disease; however, long-term comparative outcomes versus coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in real-world populations remain poorly characterised. We aimed to compare long-term all-cause mortality after PCI or CABG in Asian patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease.
METHODS: We analysed prospectively collected data from the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry, conducted at 46 hospitals in South Korea, India, Japan, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The registry enrolled adults aged 18 years or older with unprotected left main coronary artery disease (defined as a stenosis diameter of ≥50% as visually estimated on angiography), who had been treated with PCI, CABG, or medical therapy alone. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used a target trial emulation framework to compare the long-term risk of all-cause mortality between PCI with drug-eluting stents and isolated CABG. We used propensity-score overlap weighting to adjust for measured baseline covariates. The IRIS-MAIN Registry study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01341327).
FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2003, and Dec 31, 2024, 6900 patients were enrolled in the IRIS-MAIN registry, of whom 5379 (78·0%) underwent coronary revascularisation through either PCI with drug-eluting stents (3836 [71·3%]) or CABG (1543 [28·7%]) and were included in the analysis. The median duration of follow-up for all patients was 10·0 years (IQR 5·0-16·7). In the overlap-weighted population, no statistically detectable difference in 10-year weighted Kaplan-Meier rates of all-cause mortality was observed between PCI and CABG (24·0% vs 22·9%; overlap-weighted hazard ratio 1·00 [95% CI 0·87-1·14]; p=0·99). The confidence interval does not exclude a mortality benefit or harm with either strategy.
INTERPRETATION: In this non-randomised registry analysis of patients with left main coronary artery disease, there was no statistically detectable difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG. For patients considered suitable for either strategy, multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion might help patients and clinicians weigh potential trade-offs in the choice between PCI and CABG. These findings are observational and cannot establish causal treatment effects or equivalence in survival.

abstract: Long-term data on transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for significant mitral regurgitation (MR) remain limited. We aimed to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes and functional and echocardiographic findings during follow-up after MitraClip in a long-term subanalysis of the prospective multicenter GIOTTO registry. We included 406 consecutive patients undergoing MitraClip implantation for significant MR from 6 Italian centers contributing long-term follow-up. Baseline, procedural, in-hospital, and long-term follow-up data were compared according to MR etiology. Predictors of all-cause death were assessed using Cox regression analysis. Mean follow-up was 56.4±27.2 months. The cohort included 257 (63.3%) patients with functional or mixed MR and 149 (36.7%) with degenerative MR, who were older, more often female, and had smaller ventricles and higher LVEF, whereas functional or mixed MR patients had greater ischemic burden, conduction disease, prior revascularization, pacemaker implantation, and ventricular remodeling. During the overall observation period, crude all-cause death occurred in 161 patients (39.7%) and MVARC-style cardiovascular death in 98 (24.1%), without significant differences between groups. Mitral surgery, repeat TEER, endocarditis, and stroke occurred in 2.2%, 0.7%, 1.5%, and 3.5%, respectively. Among patients with available follow-up assessment, 77.5% were in NYHA class I/II. At the actual 5-year landmark echocardiographic assessment, 82.9% had none or mild MR and 97.1% had no more than moderate MR. Independent mortality predictors were older age, lower body mass index, right bundle branch block, MR etiology, larger LV end-systolic diameter, higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure, and longer index hospitalization (all p <0.05). In conclusion, in this prospective multicenter cohort, TEER with MitraClip in high-risk patients was associated with high procedural success and favorable long-term clinical and echocardiographic findings among patients with available follow-up. Mortality appeared to be associated with patient vulnerability, MR etiology, ventricular remodeling, pulmonary hypertension, and the early post-procedural course.
title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral valve regurgitation: insights from a 5-year prospective multicenter registry.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major adverse cardiovascular events arising from non-culprit lesions (NCLs) remain relevant in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), highlighting the need for more effective identification of vulnerable plaques. Although several coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived high-risk features are recognized as markers of plaque vulnerability, the significance of soft plaque morphology remains unclear. This study investigated whether ACS is associated with soft plaque morphology in NCLs on CCTA.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Overall, 174 NCLs from 69 patients with ACS or chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) who underwent CCTA within 1 month of percutaneous coronary intervention were analyzed. Soft plaques were classified according to the presence or absence of focal soft plaque thickening (FSPT), defined as localized thickening of the soft plaque component measuring ≥500 μm in at least one cross-sectional slice. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was co-registered with CCTA in 49 lesions. The soft plaque burden did not differ significantly between NCLs in patients with ACS and CCS, whereas FSPT was more frequently observed in NCLs in patients with ACS (56.4% vs. 18.8%; p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis accounting for within-patient clustering, ACS was independently associated with FSPT (odds ratio, 6.09; 95% confidence interval, 2.72-13.60; p < 0.001). On co-registered IVUS, lesions with FSPT showed larger attenuation arcs and more frequent superficial attenuation.
CONCLUSIONS: ACS was independently associated with CCTA-derived FSPT in NCLs. These exploratory findings suggest that morphological assessment of soft plaques on CCTA may provide complementary information for the characterization of NCLs. Further validation in independent cohorts is warranted.
title: Distinct soft plaque morphology on coronary computed tomography angiography in non-culprit lesions among patients with acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established genetically determined risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Whether elevated Lp(a) identifies a broader phenotype of aggressive coronary disease, integrating anatomical disease burden and recurrent clinical manifestations, remains incompletely characterised.
METHODS: We analysed 1892 patients with coronary artery disease from the multicentre CERES cohort after exclusion of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA). Lp(a) was analysed continuously, after natural-log transformation, and categorically using >50 mg/dL. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, and historical maximum LDL cholesterol (LDL-C).
RESULTS: Lp(a) was available in 1833 patients; median concentration was 24.7 [9.1-63.7] mg/dL, and 33.2% had Lp(a) >50 mg/dL. Multivessel disease was present in 50.4% and recurrent coronary events in 19.5%. Lp(a) was independently associated with multivessel disease (OR, 1.004; 95% CI, 1.001-1.006; p = 0.002) and recurrent coronary events (OR, 1.004; 95% CI, 1.001-1.006; p = 0.003). Lp(a) >50 mg/dL was associated with multivessel disease (OR, 1.406; 95% CI, 1.144-1.730; p = 0.001) and recurrent events (OR, 1.504; 95% CI, 1.166-1.942; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with greater anatomical coronary disease burden and recurrent coronary events, supporting its role as a marker of an aggressive coronary disease phenotype.
title: Lipoprotein(a) and an aggressive coronary disease phenotype: Association with multivessel disease and recurrent coronary events in the CERES study.

abstract: Early gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) cancer commonly presents without distant disease. The development of locoregional lymphadenopathy and acute pulmonary embolism raises concern for metastatic disease and may lead to inappropriate upstaging if not properly investigated. We present a 51-year-old immunocompetent Hispanic man with newly diagnosed T1a GEJ adenocarcinoma who developed FDG-avid mediastinal lymphadenopathy and an incidental subsegmental pulmonary embolism on staging computed tomography. Histological sampling via endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration revealed granulomatous inflammation without malignancy. Further workup confirmed an acute Coccidioides lymphadenitis. The patient was successfully treated with fluconazole 400 mg daily for three months, with complete radiological and endoscopic resolution. This case underscores the critical importance of histological confirmation of lymphadenopathy before attributing it to metastatic disease in early-stage GEJ cancer. Failure to consider infectious etiologies, particularly coccidioidomycosis in endemic areas or in patients with travel history, may result in unnecessary upstaging, inappropriate treatment escalation, and avoidable harm.
journal: Revista de gastroenterologia del Peru : organo oficial de la Sociedad de Gastroenterologia del Peru
title: From presumed metastasis to infection: coccidioidomycosis mimicking metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma.

abstract: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a potentially life-threatening condition that can precipitate obstructive shock, a form of circulatory failure caused by the mechanical obstruction of blood flow through the pulmonary circulation. This article explores the pathophysiological mechanisms linking massive PE to obstructive shock, highlighting key diagnostic challenges, and the importance of rapid recognition in the emergency setting. We examine current strategies for risk stratification, imaging, and laboratory testing, as well as emerging biomarkers that may aid in early identification. The article also evaluates the efficacy and limitations of therapeutic interventions, including systemic thrombolysis, catheter-directed therapies, and surgical embolectomy, in the context of hemodynamic instability. Understanding the complex interplay between PE and obstructive shock is essential for optimizing outcomes in critically ill patients.
title: Pathophysiology of Right Ventricular Failure in Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract: Acute pulmonary embolism remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with prognosis determined by right ventricular (RV) adaptation to the abrupt rise in pulmonary vascular resistance. Although most cases can be managed outside the intensive care unit, patients with RV failure, hemodynamic instability, or cardiac arrest require advanced monitoring and intervention. Management in this setting emphasizes rapid diagnosis and risk stratification, timely initiation of reperfusion therapies, and carefully tailored hemodynamic and respiratory support. Optimal outcomes rely on multidisciplinary collaboration, early escalation of care, and individualized, evidence-based decision-making.
title: Intensive Care Unit Management of the Hemodynamically Significant Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract: Catheter-directed therapies, including catheter-directed thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy, are increasingly used in patients with intermediate and high-risk pulmonary embolism. Complications, such as bleeding, vascular injury, and hemodynamic instability, require diligent preprocedural planning involving bailout strategies and the potential for extracorporeal support. We provide a pragmatic framework for appropriate patient selection of catheter-directed treatment. Although randomized data remain limited, ongoing pivotal trials will help clarify appropriate patient selection and clinical efficacy compared to anticoagulation and systemic thrombolysis alone.
title: Catheter-directed Treatment of Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract: This article summarizes the evolution of pulmonary embolism therapy, from early heparin use and landmark thrombolysis trials to modern catheter-based therapies, including catheter-directed thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. It reviews how advancements in medical and device therapies have shaped treatment selection while highlighting persistent evidence gaps. Across decades of trials, the primary challenge remains achieving balance between effective reperfusion with optimization of safety outcomes and clinical benefit.
title: Trials Review.

abstract: Pulmonary embolism is a life-threatening condition requiring prompt anticoagulation to prevent clot propagation and recurrence. Risk stratification guides therapy, with systemic thrombolysis reserved for high-risk patients and selected intermediate-high risk cases due to significant bleeding risk. Direct oral anticoagulants are preferred for most low and intermediate-low risk patients, while low-molecular-weight heparin and unfractionated heparin remain critical for higher- risk or procedurally complex cases. Emerging strategies including low-dose thrombolysis, catheter-directed therapies, and the future use of Factor XI inhibitors may improve safety without compromising efficacy. Management of bleeding complications necessitates rapid intervention, reversal when available, and coordinated multidisciplinary care.
title: Anticoagulation and Thrombolysis.

abstract: Surgical pulmonary embolectomy was once considered a salvage procedure in patients who were dying or dead. Improvements in surgical technique, technologies, and patient selection mean that surgical embolectomy is a safe procedure, potentially more effective than thrombolytics or percutaneous thrombectomy procedures. The specific patient populations who may benefit most from surgical embolectomy are discussed. The surgical technique, using cardiopulmonary bypass, is described in detail. Special situations such as clots in transit, pregnant patients with pulmonary embolism, and the emerging role of mechanical circulatory support in the management of this condition are also discussed.
title: Surgical Management of Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract: Clot in transit, defined as a mobile right heart thrombus, is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of venous thromboembolism. Its presence in acute pulmonary embolism is associated with high mortality and hemodynamic instability. Diagnosis relies primarily on echocardiography, with adjunctive roles for computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance. Management remains challenging due to the absence of randomized trials. Treatment options include anticoagulation alone, systemic thrombolysis, surgical embolectomy, and catheter-based interventions, with outcomes favoring active reperfusion in unstable patients. Multidisciplinary decision-making is essential, and ongoing research aims to clarify optimal strategies to improve survival in this high-risk population.
title: Clot in Transit.

abstract: This article highlights the limitations of thrombolysis in high-risk pulmonary embolism and the emerging role of temporary mechanical circulatory support, especially venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, as a bridge to recovery or definitive therapy. The pathophysiology of right ventricular failure in pulmonary embolism, risk stratification strategies, and decision-making frameworks for initiating mechanical circulatory support are reviewed. Further, we cover practical considerations, including device selection, circuit management during thrombectomy, and the imperative for preanesthesia planning in risk mitigation. Finally, this article highlights the importance of conducting prospective and randomized studies on device choice, timing, and integration with reperfusion strategies.
title: Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a common concern in the Emergency Department (ED) and has a wide variety of presentations. The initial stage of ED workup involves the calculation of pretest probability, using a clinical calculator or experienced clinician gestalt, and then progresses to diagnostic testing, which may involve D-Dimer measurement or radiographic imaging (typically computed tomography and ultrasonography). Management of PE depends primarily on the function of the right ventricle and the presence of shock. Low-risk PEs can be treated with outpatient oral anticoagulation, while patients who are in shock should undergo systemic thrombolysis.
title: Emergency Department Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract: Cor triatriatum sinister is an exceptionally rare congenital cardiac anomaly [1]. While restrictive forms are typically present in infancy or early childhood, survival into adolescence with a 2-3 mm fenestration is unusual [2, 3]. We report a 14-year-old male, misdiagnosed with refractory asthma for years, who presented with palpitations. Imaging and catheterisation revealed severe post-capillary pulmonary hypertension with echocardiographic evidence of right-sided chamber dilatation, D-shaped left ventricular configuration, moderate tricuspid regurgitation, and an estimated pulmonary artery pressure of 85 mmHg. Cardiac catheterisation showed PA pressure of 50/30 mmHg (mean 39 mmHg), PCWP of 28 mmHg, Qp/Qs of 1.14, and a favourable PVR/SVR ratio of 0.12, indicating reversibility. Successful surgical resection of a calcified membrane was performed via right anterolateral thoracotomy. This case underscores the importance of considering cor triatriatum sinister in adolescents with unexplained respiratory symptoms or wheezing and highlights the value of correlating echocardiographic evidence of obstruction with invasive haemodynamic assessment before surgery [4, 5].
title: A rare late presentation of restrictive cor triatriatum sinister in a 14-year-old male mimicking refractory asthma.

abstract: Fulminant myocarditis is a life-threatening inflammatory cardiac syndrome characterized by severe myocardial injury and abrupt deterioration of cardiac function, leading to rapidly progressive cardiogenic shock. Patients often require intravenous vasoactive therapy and/or temporary mechanical circulatory support to maintain systemic perfusion and prevent multiorgan failure. Although frequently preceded by a viral prodrome and affecting young and healthy individuals, fulminant myocarditis encompasses diverse etiologies, including immune-mediated and toxin-related subtypes, with major implications for diagnosis and treatment. Optimal management relies on early recognition, prompt admission to specialized cardiac intensive care units, and rapid access to advanced diagnostics, including endomyocardial biopsy and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, to confirm myocardial inflammation, exclude ischemic disease, and guide etiology-directed therapy. Hemodynamic stabilization requires tailored use of vasopressors and inotropes while minimizing catecholamine-related arrhythmias and myocardial oxygen demand. For refractory shock, early escalation to temporary mechanical circulatory support, most commonly venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, is central to restore perfusion and provide a bridge to recovery or advanced therapy. Because fulminant myocarditis frequently involves malignant arrhythmias and multiorgan dysfunction, integrated critical care management is essential. This review summarizes a practical intensive care approach to fulminant myocarditis, emphasizing early diagnosis, individualized hemodynamic and device-based support, multiorgan management, and phenotype-driven immunomodulatory treatment strategies.
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
title: Critical Care Management of Patients With Acute Fulminant Myocarditis.

abstract: ABSTRACT Fixed obstruction at the aortic isthmus may preclude transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Covered‐stent implantation can restore large‐bore access, but immediate passage of balloons and delivery systems through a newly implanted stent may expose it to longitudinal traction. Secondary stent migration during withdrawal of a valvuloplasty balloon and its intraluminal balloon‐assisted rescue have not been well characterized. An 87‐year‐old man with New York Heart Association class III symptoms had severe bicuspid aortic stenosis (peak velocity, 4.4 m/s; mean gradient, 48 mmHg; valve area, 0.65 cm2; left ventricular ejection fraction, 55%) and a focal juxtaductal aortic‐isthmus stenosis with a peak‐to‐peak gradient of 32 mmHg. Because of high surgical risk and unfavorable alternative access, same‐session covered‐stent treatment followed by transfemoral TAVR was selected. A 12 × 29‐mm Advanta V12 covered stent was deployed and flared using an 18‐mm noncompliant balloon. After aortic‐valve predilation with a 23‐mm noncompliant balloon, the stent migrated distally during balloon withdrawal. Guidewire access was preserved, and the stent remained coaxial. The balloon was recentered within the migrated stent and partially reinflated, allowing the balloon and stent to be advanced proximally as a single unit. After restoration and re‐expansion of the stent, a 23‐mm Myval valve was implanted successfully. Final transvalvular and isthmic gradients were 8 and 5 mmHg, respectively, with trivial paravalvular regurgitation and no aortic injury. The patient was discharged on day 3 and remained in NYHA class I at 6 months. Withdrawal of a large valvuloplasty balloon may cause secondary migration of a newly implanted aortic‐isthmus stent. When guidewire access, coaxial alignment, and structural integrity are preserved, controlled intraluminal balloon‐assisted repositioning may provide an effective bailout while maintaining transfemoral access.
title: Covered‐Stent Migration During Same‐Session Aortic Isthmus Repair and Bicuspid Aortic Valve TAVR

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) undergoing PCI are at high risk of restenosis and late stent thrombosis. The Firehawk stent (abluminal biodegradable‐polymer sirolimus‐eluting stent [SES]) is designed to minimize inflammation and enhance vascular healing, which may improve outcomes in patients with DM. Aims In this subgroup analysis of the TARGET All Comers trial, we compared 5‐year outcomes of patients based on diabetes status treated with the Firehawk SES versus XIENCE everolimus‐eluting stent (EES). Methods TARGET All Comers randomized patients 1:1 to Firehawk or XIENCE. In this analysis, we compare non‐stratified outcomes in DM versus non‐DM patients overall and based on stent type. The primary end point was target lesion failure (TLF) at 5 years, a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI), or ischemia‐driven target lesion revascularization (TLR). Secondary end points included components of the primary outcome and definite/probable stent thrombosis. Results Of the 1651 patients enrolled, 388 (23%) had DM (197 Firehawk and 191 XIENCE) and 1263 (77%) had no DM (624 Firehawk and 639 XIENCE). Patients with DM were older, had more hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and more prior coronary interventions. Compared with non‐DM patients, TLF ( p < 0.001), cardiac death ( p < 0.001), TVMI ( p = 0.002), ischemia‐driven TLR ( p < 0.001), and definite/probable stent thrombosis ( p = 0.008) were more frequent in patients with DM. There were no differences in primary or secondary end points between Firehawk and XIENCE in patients with or without DM. Conclusion This subgroup analysis of the multicenter TARGET All Comers trial shows that at 5 years, the rate of TLF among patients with DM was similar with the Firehawk SES and the XIENCE EES. Our analysis demonstrates that regardless of stent type, patients with DM have higher rates of TLF.
title: Final 5‐Year Results of Abluminal Groove‐Filled Biodegradable‐Polymer Sirolimus‐Eluting Stent Versus Durable‐Polymer Everolimus‐Eluting Stent in Patients With Diabetes: Results of the TARGET AC Trial

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dual‐lumen microcatheters (DLMs) are adjunctive devices that has been increasingly incorporated into contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). These catheters contain two independent working lumens, a rapid‐exchange (RX) port and an over‐the‐wire (OTW) port, within a single low‐profile shaft, permitting guidewire advancement and exchange within a shared working space. Published consensus documents have focused predominantly on chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions, with less on non‐CTO lesions. Methods This narrative review describes five practical applications of DLMs in non‐CTO lesions. For each technique, we outlined the procedural rationale, a stepwise approach, and technical considerations. Results Five applications are presented: (1) aorto‐ostial wiring in the setting of a protruding ostial stent or anomalous coronary takeoff; (2) reverse wiring of a side branch with an acute or angulated takeoff; (3) side‐branch re‐entry after stent deployment; (4) contrast injection through the OTW port; and (5) parallel wiring for complex lesions. Conclusions DLMs offer several practical applications beyond CTO PCI. Familiarity with these techniques and their technical considerations may help operators select and apply DLM‐assisted strategies in complex non‐CTO lesions.
title: Dual‐Lumen Microcatheters in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Five Useful Techniques to Facilitate Coronary Wiring in Non‐CTO Lesions
