abstract: Management of prehospital hemorrhagic shock and traumatic cardiac arrest remains a critical capability gap in trauma resuscitation. Hybrid endovascular and extracorporeal technologies and techniques are evolving to meet the challenges of noncompressible hemorrhage, tissue perfusion, gas exchange, and metabolic derangement correction in the setting of complex traumatic injuries and aim to improve patient outcomes by augmenting the capabilities of interdisciplinary trauma/critical care resuscitation teams. The clinical value of these emerging technological advancements depends upon matching the intervention(s) to the dominant physiological failure modes while assisting in damage control surgery and definitive surgical repair. This narrative review discusses advancements in resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) and inferior vena cava (REBOVC), selective regional perfusion, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), and the technical and logistical barriers facing their clinical implementation. An escalating care pathway and conceptual framework to manage noncompressible hemorrhage and hemorrhage-induced traumatic cardiac arrest utilizing an integrated endovascular and extracorporeal approach is proposed based on prior literature and recent developments in selective abdominopelvic perfusion. Market dynamics remain an important consideration for fielding new technologies; development of specialized medical devices would benefit from versatile, multi-use capabilities to serve broader patient populations to enable economically sustainable employment within healthcare systems.
title: Endovascular and Extracorporeal Management of Complex Traumatic Injuries: Emerging Technologies and Techniques

abstract: The current definitions, explanations, and clinical classification of angina pectoris, particularly the traditional definitions of "typical" and “atypical” angina or chest pain and the stable versus unstable dichotomy, contains conceptual inconsistencies that impair understanding concepts, diagnostic clarity and clinical decision-making. This article challenges several long-standing assumptions about angina, especially regarding the "typical angina" construct and unstable angina definition. We argue for a redefinition grounded in pathophysiology of ischemia and clinical logic rather than rigid historical formulas. These criticisms carry important implications for both education and practice.
title: Rethinking Angina Pectoris—Toward Conceptual and Diagnostic Clarity

abstract: Abstract Objective: To investigate the correlation between melanoma inhibitory activity 3 (MIA3) and coronary collateral circulation (CCC) formation in patients with coronary chronic total occlusion (CTO). Methods: A total of 489 patients with CTO admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University from January 2021 to July 2022 were enrolled as study subjects. According to the Rentrop classification system, patients were divided into a poor CCC group and a good CCC group. Baseline clinical data were collected, and plasma levels of MIA3 and vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) were quantitatively measured. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent factors correlated with good CCC formation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted to evaluate the clinical value of predicting good CCC formation. The net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were calculated to assess the incremental predictive performance of MIA3 when added to traditional risk models. Clinical subgroup and interaction analyses were also performed. Results: Compared with the poor CCC group, patients in the good CCC group showed significantly higher plasma MIA3 levels (1280.87 pg/ml vs.1041.30 pg/ml, P 1462.24pg/ml) was identified as an independent related factor for good CCC formation (OR= 3.152, P Conclusion: MIA3 is an independent protective factor for good CCC formation in patients with CTO. Higher MIA3 levels are correlated with better collateral development, and this association is particularly prominent in patients with dyslipidemia. Incorporating MIA3 into traditional clinical models significantly enhances the predictive performance for good CCC formation in CTO patients.
title: Association Between MIA3 and Coronary Collateral Circulation Formation in Patients with Chronic Total Occlusion

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) face complex physical, psychosocial, and self-management demands, yet their stage-specific symptoms and care needs across the PCI pathway remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to map these stage-specific experiences and construct a patient journey map to inform tailored nursing care. Methods Guided by the Timing It Right (TIR) framework, we conducted a qualitative descriptive study using maximum-variation purposive sampling. Sixteen patients with CMM undergoing PCI were recruited from the Department of Cardiology at a tertiary hospital in Wuhan, China, from June to July 2026 and participated in 20 semi-structured interviews. Qualitative content analysis used four prespecified journey-map domains with inductive development of subthemes, which were synthesized into a patient journey map. Results The PCI pathway was represented by three phases: preprocedural preparation, postprocedural recovery, and transition. Forty-eight subthemes were identified across four domains: symptoms, care needs, emotions, and pain points. Preprocedural accounts emphasized symptom recognition, gaps in chronic disease self-management, and needs for procedural information and reassurance; postprocedural accounts centered on symptom burden, prognostic uncertainty, and rehabilitation support; before discharge, patients anticipated difficulties coordinating multimorbidity self-management and expressed needs for structured, multidisciplinary continuity of care. Conclusions The journey map identified distinct stage-specific patterns in symptoms, emotions, care needs, and pain points among patients with CMM undergoing PCI. These findings may help align nursing support with preprocedural information and reassurance needs, postprocedural symptom and rehabilitation needs, and pre-discharge preparation for coordinated multimorbidity self-management.
title: Symptom-Demand journey map for patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity undergoing the periprocedural pathway of percutaneous coronary intervention: A qualitative study

abstract: Abstract Background Slow flow/no-reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a common complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and is associated with larger infarct size and worse outcomes, yet simple tools for pre-procedural risk estimation remain limited. We investigated whether the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) independently predicts slow flow/no-reflow after PCI in patients with AMI, and whether adding high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and culprit-vessel location improves prediction. Methods This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with AMI who underwent PCI between January 2023 and December 2025. Slow flow/no-reflow was defined as a post-procedural Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) flow grade of 2 or less in the culprit vessel. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); the combined model was compared with NLR alone using paired bootstrap testing of the AUC difference and a nested likelihood-ratio test. Internal validation used bootstrap optimism correction and 10-fold cross-validation. Results Of 305 patients, 53 (17.4%) developed slow flow/no-reflow. Log-transformed NLR (odds ratio [OR] 1.88, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22–2.88, P = 0.004) and log-transformed hs-cTnI (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.01–1.53, P = 0.043) were independent risk factors, whereas a left anterior descending culprit vessel, including the left main, was inversely associated with slow flow/no-reflow (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.22–0.86, P = 0.016). The combined model achieved an AUC of 0.735 (95% CI 0.659–0.805) versus 0.674 for NLR alone (ΔAUC 0.061, 95% CI 0.003–0.123, P = 0.039); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.719 and the 10-fold cross-validated AUC 0.722, and calibration was good (Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.101). Adding thrombus burden, left ventricular ejection fraction, AMI type, age, or sex did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC ≤ 0.002). Conclusions NLR is an independent risk factor for slow flow/no-reflow after PCI in patients with AMI. Combining NLR with hs-cTnI and culprit-vessel location adds discriminative value that is retained after internal validation. NLR is easy to obtain at admission and may support pre-procedural risk stratification, but external validation is needed before clinical use.
title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as an independent risk factor for slow flow/no-reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute myocardial infarction: a single-center retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an effective treatment for severely calcified coronary lesions during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, data regarding patient-reported pain and anxiety during IVL are limited. Objective: To compare pain and anxiety levels in patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI with those undergoing conventional PCI. Methods In this prospective single-center observational study, 100 patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing PCI between 2024 and 2025 were enrolled. Fifty patients underwent IVL-assisted PCI and 50 underwent conventional PCI. Pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, while anxiety was assessed using the Subjective Units of Distress Scale (SUDS). Results Baseline demographic characteristics were similar between groups. The IVL group had more complex coronary artery disease, including a higher prevalence of three-vessel disease (70% vs. 38%, p = 0.001), more previous coronary angiographies ( p = 0.007), and higher radiation exposure ( p = 0.018). Despite greater lesion complexity, no significant differences were observed in pain or anxiety scores between groups. The number of IVL pulses was not associated with pain or anxiety. Conclusions IVL-assisted PCI was not associated with increased pain or anxiety compared with conventional PCI despite greater procedural complexity. These findings support IVL as a well-tolerated strategy for the treatment of severely calcified coronary lesions.
title: Pain and Anxiety During Intravascular Lithotripsy-Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Compared with Conventional PCI: A Prospective Single-Center Observational Study

abstract: Abstract INTRODUCTION Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with revascularization procedures such as coronary artery bypass grafting and percutaneous coronary intervention being commonly performed interventions. Despite these procedures, patients frequently experience diminished functional capacity and quality of life. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a proven strategy for improving post-surgical outcomes, yet participation remains notably low in low-resource settings such as Pakistan. METHODS This comparative study enrolled 501 post-revascularization patients at a tertiary cardiac care center in Karachi, Pakistan between January 2020 and December 2022. Participants were categorized into attenders (n = 250) who completed ≥ 15 structured CR sessions within 8 weeks, and non-attenders (n = 251) who attended fewer sessions. Exercise capacity was measured using peak metabolic equivalents, while exercise duration was assessed as moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in minutes per week. Assessments were conducted at baseline, 8-week follow-up, and one-year follow-up. Non-parametric statistical tests including Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U tests were employed for analysis. RESULTS Both groups demonstrated improvements in peak metabolic equivalents and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity from baseline to follow-up. However, CR attenders showed significantly greater median improvements in peak metabolic equivalents (1.41 vs 0.76, p CONCLUSION Structured CR significantly enhances exercise capacity and physical activity duration in post-revascularization patients, with attenders demonstrating substantially greater improvements than non-attenders. These findings underscore the vital role of organized CR in optimizing recovery outcomes in low-resource settings and support the expansion of such programs in Pakistan.

abstract: Abstract Myocardial ischaemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is a major cause of residual myocardial damage following coronary revascularisation. Unfortunately, effective mechanism-based pharmacological interventions that can be translated into clinical practice remain limited. Emerging evidence indicates that ferroptosis and inflammation mutually reinforce each other and constitute a critical pathological process responsible for the amplification of myocardial injury during the early phase of reperfusion. Upon myocardial reperfusion, ferroptotic cardiomyocytes release damage-associated molecular patterns and disrupt tissue barriers, thereby activating the innate immune system and initiating inflammatory responses. In turn, inflammation promotes oxidative stress, dysregulation of iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation through the activation of inflammatory signaling pathways and the release of pro-inflammatory mediators, ultimately exacerbating ferroptosis. This reciprocal interaction establishes a self-perpetuating vicious cycle that contributes to the progression of MIRI. Encouragingly, several Western medicines and bioactive compounds derived from traditional Chinese medicine have shown therapeutic potential in modulating MIRI. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying the bidirectional interaction between ferroptosis and inflammation in MIRI and discusses emerging pharmacological strategies targeting this pathological network. Collectively, the available evidence suggests that future therapeutic approaches to MIRI should extend beyond reperfusion therapy, antioxidant treatment, or anti-inflammatory intervention alone and instead consider combined strategies that simultaneously suppress inflammation and ferroptosis. Such an integrated approach may provide a novel translational framework for early risk assessment, therapeutic response prediction and targeted intervention in patients with MIRI.
title: Targeting Ferroptosis-Inflammation Crosstalk: A Novel Strategy for the Prevention and Treatment of Myocardial Ischaemia Reperfusion Injury

abstract: Background: Cardiovascular interventions may impact both left ventricular mass (LVM) and end-diastolic volume (EDV), but the net effect on wall thickness has been difficult to accurately evaluate. Global average left ventricular end-diastolic wall thickness (GT) relates non-linearly to LVM and EDV. We hypothesized that if GT is independent of EDV in health, then GT will be an ideal measure of post-intervention change in left ventricular hypertrophy. Methods: GT [mm] was calculated using LVM and EDV by cardiovascular magnetic resonance as previously validated. The correlation between GT and EDV was evaluated in healthy volunteers. Change in GT following intervention was evaluated for aortic stenosis undergoing valve replacement, hypertension commencing antihypertensive medications, athletes undergoing forced detraining, and aortic regurgitation undergoing valve replacement. The performance of GT was compared to LVM/EDV. Results: Among healthy volunteers (n=4461, mean+/-SD age 59+/-10 years, 50% female), EDV correlated with LVM/EDV but negligibly with GT (R2>0.16 vs R2<0.02, p<0.001 for both sexes). GT and not LVM/EDV changed after intervention in all conditions (p[≤]0.02 for all). Post-intervention changes in GT varied by condition (mean+/-SEM aortic stenosis [n=102]: -1.75+/-0.13mm, hypertension [n=78]: -0.66+/-0.08mm, athletes [n=28]: -0.29+/-0.09mm, aortic regurgitation [n=58]: +0.50+/-0.11 mm, p[≤]0.02 for all comparisons). Conclusions: In health, GT, unlike LVM/EDV, remains effectively unchanged across EDV values, indicating that GT is a physiological constant in health and can track pathological changes. After intervention, only GT and not LVM/EDV consistently changed. Instead of LVM/EDV, GT should be used to quantify remodelling after interventions in left ventricular hypertrophy.
title: Global thickness for accurate and precise evaluation of post-intervention remodelling in left ventricular hypertrophy
